gloss: to come in; to flow in; to enter (toward the speaker)

definitions.gloss: to come in; to enter (moving toward the speaker or scene)
definitions.explanation: Compound of {入|はい}る (to enter) + くる (to come). Expresses the movement of something entering a space from outside, with the directional sense of movement toward the speaker or the focal scene. Used for people, air, light, information, or other things flowing in.

examples.japanese: {冷気|れいき}が{窓|まど}から{入|はい}ってくる。
examples.english: Cold air comes in through the window.

examples.japanese: {誰|だれ}かが{部屋|へや}に{入|はい}ってきた。
SNSを{通|とお}じて{海外|かいがい}からも{情報|じょうほう}が{入|はい}ってくるようになった。
examples.english: Information has come to flow in from overseas through social media as well.

notes:
The ～てくる pattern attached to {入|はい}る conveys that the entering is directed toward the speaker or scene. Compare {入|はい}っていく (to go in, moving away) and {入|はい}る (neutral).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {部屋|へや}に{入|はい}ってくる: to come into the room
- {情報|じょうほう}が{入|はい}ってくる: information comes in
- {光|ひかり}が{入|はい}ってくる: light comes in
- {風|かぜ}が{入|はい}ってくる: a breeze comes in

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {入|はい}る: to enter — neutral, no directional connotation
- {入|はい}っていく: to go in — the movement is away from the speaker
